currentUse: St. Luke Parish ended as a distinct institution in the Diocese of Pittsburgh's 1994 merger that created Ave Maria Parish. The former St. Luke church at 126 Church Street was retained and renamed Ave Maria Church. Ave Maria Parish then entered the distinct Saint Katharine Drexel Parish in 2017. The Diocese currently lists Ave Maria Church at that address as an active Saint Katharine Drexel worship site, with a Saturday Mass. This is building and worship-site continuity, not survival of St. Luke as a parish.
summary: St. Luke was a mixed Roman Catholic parish founded in Bentleyville in 1903 to serve Polish, Lithuanian, and other local Catholics. Diocesan history records Polish, Lithuanian, and English worship through 1935. A contemporary 1914 Lithuanian report says local Lithuanians lacked their own national parish and priest, so the record is classified as a mixed parish with documented Lithuanian ministry rather than an exclusively Lithuanian national parish. After two unsuccessful worship sites, a brick church was begun in 1908 and dedicated on February 15, 1909. St. Luke merged into Ave Maria Parish in 1994; Ave Maria merged into Saint Katharine Drexel Parish in 2017. The former St. Luke building survives as the active Ave Maria Church at 126 Church Street.

historicalNarrative.text: The Diocese of Pittsburgh dates St. Luke Parish to 1903 and describes a mixed congregation in Bentleyville. Its history says worship was conducted in Polish, Lithuanian, and English until 1935. A manually reviewed Draugas report from August 6, 1914 adds an important class boundary: it says Lithuanians in Bentleyville and Ellsworth had neither a priest of their nationality nor a Lithuanian parish. Together, the sources establish a Roman Catholic parish with Lithuanian participation and language ministry, but not a separately erected Lithuanian national parish.

historicalNarrative.text: The parish used two early sites unsuccessfully before building the durable brick church. The diocesan account records the cornerstone in 1908 and dedication on February 15, 1909. The current diocesan directory identifies the surviving site as Ave Maria Church, 126 Church Street, Bentleyville. No separate street address for either temporary predecessor site has been established.

historicalNarrative.text: On February 12, 1994, St. Luke joined St. Clement in Ellsworth and St. Joseph in Cokeburg to form the distinct Ave Maria Parish. The merger ended St. Luke's separate institutional life, while its church continued as Ave Maria's Bentleyville worship site. This is a typed merger relationship and a retained-site relationship; it must not be described as an uninterrupted St. Luke parish.

historicalNarrative.text: Ave Maria merged with four other parishes on January 8, 2017 to form Saint Katharine Drexel Parish. The Diocese's current directory lists Ave Maria Church at 126 Church Street as an active Saint Katharine Drexel site and publishes a Saturday Mass there. That dated official listing directly supports the top-level standing label as of the case date. It establishes present Catholic use of the former St. Luke structure, not institutional survival of either St. Luke or Ave Maria Parish.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The public registry's Lithuanian association is retained but narrowed: a contemporary 1914 report explicitly says Bentleyville and Ellsworth Lithuanians did not have a Lithuanian parish, while the Diocese documents Lithuanian-language worship inside mixed St. Luke. St. Luke, Ave Maria, and Saint Katharine Drexel are three distinct institutions; continuity at 126 Church Street does not collapse their merger chain.
gaps: The canonical erection instrument, identities and addresses of the two earliest worship sites, full construction contract and deed history, Lithuanian-language schedule after 1935, sacramental-record custody, and any cemetery relationship remain unresolved. Current official use establishes that the 1908-1909 structure stands, but a structural survey and parcel-level ownership history were not located.
